title: Free categorical algebras and their forgetful functor
statement:
Use [def-coef-complete-algebroid] for universes, monoidal infinity-categories, categorical algebras, and presentability. Let $\mathcal V$ be a presentably monoidal infinity-category, with tensor preserving small colimits separately, and let $S$ be a small set. Let $\mathcal A_S=\operatorname{Alg}_{\Delta_S^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mathcal V)$ denote categorical algebras with object set $S$, and let $V_S:\mathcal A_S\to\mathcal V^{S^2}$ evaluate an algebra on its mapping objects $A(s,t)$. Then $\mathcal A_S$ is presentable; $V_S$ is conservative, preserves geometric realizations and all small sifted colimits, and has a left adjoint $G_S$. Here conservative means reflecting equivalences, geometric realization means a colimit indexed by $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, and sifted means that indexed colimits of spaces commute with finite products. The underlying graph of the free algebra is naturally
$$V_SG_S(P)(s,t)\simeq\coprod_{n\geq0}\ \coprod_{s=x_0,\ldots,x_n=t}P(x_0,x_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes P(x_{n-1},x_n).$$
For $n=0$ the summand is the tensor unit when $s=t$ and is absent otherwise. Its composition concatenates paths in this forward tensor order and its adjunction unit inserts length-one paths. More precisely, the adjunct $G_S(P)\to A$ of a graph map $u:P\to V_S(A)$, restricted to a path summand, is the tensor of the maps $u(x_{i-1},x_i)$ followed by the coherently specified iterated composition of $A$; on a length-zero summand it is the identity-object map of $A$. These formulas describe a coherent natural transformation on the whole graph infinity-category, not just a map of homotopy categories.

source.place: Gepner–Haugseng, Enriched infinity-categories via nonsymmetric infinity-operads, v4 (2019), Theorem A.4.6, Proposition A.4.9, Corollary A.5.4, Lemma A.5.5, Corollary A.5.7, printed pp. 92–94. Applied to the categorical operad as explicitly explained in Haugseng, Rectification of enriched infinity-categories, Proposition 5.2(a),(b),(d),(f), https://arxiv.org/html/1312.3881v4. Haugseng cites the older numbering B.4.6, B.4.9, B.5.4, B.5.5, B.5.7. Both sources read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this homotopy-coherent theorem.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal M=\Delta_S^{\mathrm{op}}$. In the relative-nerve model of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], all simplices valued in the discrete set $S^{n+1}$ are constant; its compatibility equations say exactly that a base order map selects the appropriate entries. Thus this model is the nerve of the category of lists. Its objects over $[n]$ are lists $(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$; projection records $[n]$ and an order map selects or repeats the listed entries. Consequently $\mathcal M_{[0]}=S$, $\mathcal M_{[1]}=S^2$, and its generalized Segal maps identify a list with its consecutive pairs over their matching endpoints. This is a small generalized nonsymmetric operad with discrete, hence space-valued, zero-fiber. The inert-algebra identification in [lem-coef-free-operadic-active-slice-formula] identifies restriction $\tau^*$ with the stated graph functor $V_S$, since a functor out of the discrete set $S^2$ is exactly a family $P(s,t)$.

Apply [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability] to $\mathcal M$ to obtain presentability of $\mathcal A_S$. By [lem-coef-free-operadic-active-slice-formula], the inert part $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}$ is again a small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad and the inert inclusion $\tau:\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}\to\mathcal M$ preserves inert arrows and is the identity over $[0]$, so both zero-fibers are the space $S$. Here this is also visible directly: a morphism of $\mathcal M$ lies over a map $\phi^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\phi:[m]\to[n]$, and all the composites with the inert projections to $[1]$ are inert exactly when $\phi(i)=\phi(i-1)+1$ for all $i$, that is, when $\phi$ is inert; so the generalized Segal decomposition of mapping spaces restricts to $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}$, and inner horn fillers and inert cocartesian lifts stay in $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}$ because inert maps are closed under composition and $\psi\circ\rho$ inert with $\rho$ inert forces $\psi$ inert. Thus the first, generalized-operad clause of [lem-coef-operadic-free-extension] gives $\tau_!\dashv\tau^*$. With the graph identification in step 1 set $G_S=\tau_!$. All required colimits are small, since $S$ and the category of finite lists in $S$ are small; the separately colimit-preserving tensor hypothesis is exactly the compatibility hypothesis for this free extension.

Apply [lem-coef-operadic-colorwise-sifted-colimits] to this same $\mathcal M$. A map of algebras is an equivalence precisely when every map $A(s,t)\to B(s,t)$ is one, proving conservativity of $V_S$. For a small sifted diagram, its colimit algebra has $(s,t)$-component the colimit of the corresponding graph components. Hence $V_S$ preserves every small sifted colimit, including the geometric realizations explicitly covered by that lemma. No colimit assertion for all arbitrary graph diagrams is needed.

For $c=(s,t)$ compute the active slices in [lem-coef-free-operadic-active-slice-formula]. An object of $\mathcal P^{\mathcal M}_{c,n}$ is exactly a list $(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ with $x_0=s$ and $x_n=t$: the unique active map is opposite to the endpoint-preserving map $[1]\to[n]$. A morphism in this fixed-arity slice lies over an inert endomorphism of $[n]$, which must be the identity; the fibers are discrete, so there are no other morphisms. Thus the slice is the discrete set of these paths. Its tensor diagram assigns $P(x_0,x_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes P(x_{n-1},x_n)$. Substituting into the active-slice formula replaces its inner colimit by the coproduct over paths and gives exactly the displayed formula in the statement. When $n=0$ there is one path only if $s=t$, contributing the empty tensor $\mathbf1$; otherwise this indexing set is empty.

source.place: Definition A.4.8 and Proposition A.4.9; Definition 4.1.1.

proof.text: The arity-one identity operation at $(s,t)$ is the path $(s,t)$; therefore the unit in [lem-coef-free-operadic-active-slice-formula] inserts the length-one summand. For paths $s=x_0,\ldots,x_n=t$ and $t=y_0,\ldots,y_m=u$, substitution of their active operations has list $(x_0,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_m)$. The substitution clause of that lemma therefore identifies composition on these summands with concatenation, in the forward tensor order inherited from the consecutive inert colors. The arity-zero operation inserts the length-zero path. Associativity and units are compatible with every further substitution because the same concatenated list results, and the associators and unitors are those of the monoidal infinity-category; their coherences are included in the operadic substitution clause.

source.place: Proposition A.4.9 together with Definition A.4.1 (operadic free algebra).

proof.text: Given $u:P\to V_S(A)$, apply the adjunct-cocone description in [lem-coef-free-operadic-active-slice-formula]. On the path of step 4 it tensors the maps $u(x_{i-1},x_i)$ in their listed order and then applies $A$ to the active arrow of that list, which is precisely the coherently specified iterated composition of $A$. For a length-zero path this is its nullary identity-object map. The mapping-space equivalences of [lem-coef-operadic-free-extension] identify this cocone map with the adjunct, not merely a homotopy-category representative. The naturality and substitution compatibility in the active-slice lemma apply to the whole functor infinity-category of graphs, so these formulas are coherent natural transformations for graph maps and all their higher homotopies, as required.

source.place: Propositions A.4.3 and A.4.9; Haugseng, Rectification, Proposition 5.2(f) for the path specialization.

No duplicate found, and neither new node restates a clause of the item. The math checks out: the relative nerve of discrete S^{n+1} is the category of lists; the generalized Segal condition holds with zero-fiber S; equivalences and sifted colimits are colorwise (a sifted K is weakly contractible, which covers arity 0); a fixed-arity active slice is the discrete set of endpoint-fixed paths, since inert endomorphisms of [n] are identities; composition is concatenation in forward order; the adjunct is the tensor of the u's followed by A(alpha). Small cases: S empty (both categories are a point), |S|=1 (tensor algebra), s!=t with n=0 (no summand), all entries initial. The DAG stays acyclic. Every citation is in the unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, so no tool_uses are needed. No SGA. Item statement unchanged. Repairs (2): (1) B2/E1: lem-coef-free-operadic-active-slice-formula never said that M is a generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad, and used the free-extension adjunction for tau without stating that tau meets its hypotheses. Fixed by adding the hypothesis and a clause that M_triv is again a small generalized operad with the same zero-fiber and that tau is the identity over [0]. (2) E1: item step 2 did not check that M_triv is a generalized operad before applying the first clause of free-extension. Fixed by citing the new clause and adding the direct check (composites with the inert projections are inert iff phi is inert, so Segal restricts; inner horns fill; inert cocartesian lifts stay cocartesian). Caveat: the network is blocked here, so I could not open Gepner-Haugseng 1312.3178 or Haugseng 1312.3881; I checked their uses by my own derivation, not by the printed numbering (A.4.6/A.4.9/A.5.4/A.5.5/A.5.7).
